info.title: BytNode Crypto Market Data API
info.summary: Crypto market data aggregated across the major venues, derivatives, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain — for developers and AI agents.
info.description:
**BytNode is a crypto market-data API built for developers and AI agents.** One key gives you market data aggregated across the major crypto venues, derivatives positioning, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain fundamentals — 132 REST routes, a consolidated real-time WebSocket and a native MCP server, all behind one consistent contract.

## Why BytNode

- **Aggregated across the major venues, not one exchange.** Spot and perpetual futures markets are consolidated into one number per metric: volumes are summed, rates are open-interest weighted, prices volume weighted — and the method is documented for every metric.
- **Depth on the assets that matter.** 22 pairs: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, TRX, SUI, HYPE, XLM, XMR, LINK, ADA, LTC, UNI, GRAM (ex-TON), AVAX, HBAR, NEAR, TAO, plus USDC and USDT spot pairs. This is a deliberate choice: together these assets are about 93 % of the total crypto market capitalisation (measured on 2026-09-30: 2.69 of 2.88 trillion USD), and each of them gets every family of data from every venue that lists it — quality and depth on the assets people actually trade, instead of thin coverage of thousands of tickers.
- **Twelve data families in one API.** Prices and candles, individual trades, order book, order flow (CVD, trade candles), funding, basis, open interest, liquidations and liquidation heatmap, tokenomics, sentiment, macro (FRED + intraday), spot ETF fundamentals (SEC EDGAR), options (OI, IV, max pain, greeks), Bitcoin network, Ethereum fundamentals, on-chain valuation, and 19 server-side technical indicators. Many providers sell these as separate products; here they share one key, one envelope and one set of conventions.
- **Honest numbers.** Every bucketed or history row says whether it is final (`is_closed`); every empty answer says why (`unavailable`: `not_applicable`, `no_api_key`, `no_data`); every numeric field has a documented unit.
- **Made for AI agents.** A native MCP server (3 tools, 60 fields), `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, this OpenAPI contract with units and real examples, one-request snapshots of up to 48 fields, and stable machine-readable error codes.
- **Priced for builders.** A free plan (10,000 requests/month), then Traders from 6.95 USD/month, Financial from 19.95 USD/month and Startup from 99.95 USD/month (billed yearly), with history depth and families growing with the plan. See https://bytnode.com/pricing. Each operation names its data family in `x-family` (the identifiers `GET /v1/limits` returns for your key); `x-metered: false` marks the routes that are never counted.

## Quick start

1. Create a free key at https://bytnode.com/sign-up.
2. Send it in the `X-API-KEY` header:

```
curl -H "X-API-KEY: $BYTNODE_API_KEY" "https://api.bytnode.com/v1/funding/rate?symbol=BTCUSDT"
```

## Conventions

- **Envelope.** Every success is `{status: "ok", server_time, data_type, data}`, plus the effective `symbol`, `timeframe`, `asset`, `series`, `market` or filter (`expiry`, `ticker`, `dataset`, `category`) when the route has them. `status` is `ok` whenever the request succeeded (the state of the feeds is `data.state` on `/v1/status`). The shape of `data` follows the path: an OBJECT (or `null`) for the latest value of a metric — `/v1/klines` is the latest closed candle; a LIST (most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`) for every `/history` route and for the event series `/v1/trades/{spot,futures,large}`, `/v1/trades-kline/futures/seconds` and `/v1/liquidations/events`. A list carries `step`, the step between its rows (`1h` when you asked `timeframe=1h`; `1d` for a daily series, `8h` for funding, `1m` for the Bitcoin fee readings): a bucket row is dated at the start of its bucket, a periodic reading at its own instant; `timeframe` is only ever the parameter you sent. Collections are lists too: `/v1/symbols`, `/v1/etf/fundamentals`, `/v1/macro/series`, `/v1/macro/intraday/series`, and the options expiry, max-pain and OI distribution routes. A field that can be `null` is typed so in the schema; any other field is never `null`.
- **Units.** `*_pct` = percent (58.5 = 58.5 %), `*_ratio` = a dimensionless quotient that names what it divides (`put_call_ratio` 1.2 = 1.2 puts per call, `big_small_ratio`; a share of a whole is a fraction, 0.585 = 58.5 %), `*_bps` = basis points, `*_usd` = USD (every USD amount ends in `_usd`), `*_s` = seconds (every duration), `*_count` = a count, `*_pp` = percentage points. Prices, and price differences such as `basis_value`, are in the quote currency (USDT for BTCUSDT). Volumes and quantities (`volume`, `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, `net_volume`, `oi`, `holdings`...) are in BASE ASSET units (BTC for BTCUSDT), never dollars: a quantity OF AN ASSET without a unit suffix is in base asset units; any other measure (virtual bytes, difficulty, block height, index points) states its unit in `x-unit`. A name without a market suffix covers EVERY market of the route: on a candle, `volume` is spot + perpetual futures, `volume_spot` and `volume_futures` one market each; the candle's prices (`open`... `close`) are those of one reference spot market. Every response schema carries each field's unit in `x-unit`; `x-units` at the root maps a field NAME to its unit only when that unit is the same on every route. Numbers are rounded to 12 significant digits.
- **Names.** One concept has one name on every route, in the snapshot, in the MCP and on the WebSocket: `buy_volume` / `sell_volume` / `net_volume`, `trade_count`, `sample_count`, booleans `is_*`, a qualitative reading `label` (`put_call_label` for the put/call reading), instants `*_at`, durations `*_s`, counts `*_count`, a value at the start of a window `previous_*`, a running total `*_cumulative`, a change over time `*_change*`; the perpetual market is `futures` everywhere and the order book is `orderbook` everywhere (REST, snapshot, WebSocket `orderbook.*`). A TRADE is one execution (`/v1/trades/spot`, `/v1/trades/futures`, WebSocket `trades.*`, plan family `trades`); the candles aggregated from trades are `trades_kline` (`/v1/trades-kline`). A path uses the name of its fields (`/v1/oi/change` serves `oi_change`, `/v1/options/put-call-ratio` serves `put_call_ratio`); a ratio route is `<a>-<b>-ratio`; Bitcoin lives under `/v1/btc/*` and Ethereum under `/v1/eth/*`. `data_type` is the route's own name (`/v1/trades/avg-size/history` -> `trades_avg_size_history`), and a snapshot field is named after the route that serves the same data (`liquidations_cumulative`, `trades_kline@1h`).
- **Market in the path.** A route that serves several markets takes the market as a path suffix: no suffix = every market (spot + perpetual futures), `/spot`, `/futures` (`/v1/cvd`, `/v1/cvd/spot`, `/v1/cvd/futures`; the same for `/v1/buy-sell-ratio`, `/v1/trades/avg-size`, `/v1/orderbook`, `/v1/trades-kline`). The envelope repeats it in `market`. A route on ONE market says it in its path or its description and repeats it in `market` too: `/v1/trades/large` (large trades are perpetual futures trades), `/v1/trades-kline/futures/seconds`.
- **Time.** Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-09-28T14:00:00.000Z`). `time` is the canonical key: every timestamped object under `data` carries it. It follows ONE of two rules, and the description of `time` on each route says which. (1) A BUCKET (candles, trade candles, CVD, order book per bucket, funding per 8-hour period, every `/history` row, and the latest value of a bucketed route: `/v1/klines`, `/v1/cvd`, `/v1/buy-sell-ratio`, `/v1/trades/avg-size`, `/v1/liquidations/big-small-ratio`, `/v1/orderbook`, `/v1/spread/interexchange`, `/v1/trades-kline`: each one requires `timeframe` and returns the first row of its `/history`) is dated at its START and carries `is_closed`. (2) A POINT-IN-TIME value is dated at the instant it refers to: the END of a rolling window — and only a rolling window carries `window_start_at` and `window_s` (`/v1/liquidations/cumulative`, `/v1/oi/change`, `/v1/funding/cumulative`, `/v1/options/oi/change`) — the instant of the computation (`/v1/basis`), the instant the SOURCE states (options, BTC, ETH, tokenomics; `/v1/global`, which may end in `.999`), the settlement a forecast is for (`/v1/funding/next`), the EVENT (trades, large trades, liquidations), and the most recent input of a composite (`/v1/macro/correlations`, `/momentum`, `/risk`, which also give `oldest_input_date`). A daily value is dated at midnight UTC. The envelope's `server_time` is the time of the response. Time bounds (`since_ms`, `until_ms`) are epoch MILLISECONDS, inclusive; `since_ms=0` means "from the start of the data".
- **Closed buckets.** Bucketed routes serve the last CLOSED bucket. `?live=1` adds the open one with `is_closed: false` on the routes that declare it: `/v1/klines`, `/v1/cvd`, `/v1/trades-kline` (and their `/spot` and `/futures` variants), `/v1/funding/rate` and `/v1/spread/interexchange`; elsewhere it is an unknown parameter (422). A bucket appears once its inputs are settled, a few seconds after its end (about 2 s for a 1m order book, 5 s for a 1m candle; 20 s at most when a venue is late). Every bucket row carries `is_closed`; a rolling-window value is always final and carries none.
- **Pagination.** Every paged route speaks one dialect: `next` is the relative URL of the following page, ready to call (`/v1/klines/history?symbol=BTCUSDT&timeframe=1h&limit=100&before_ms=…`), or `null` once the range is read. Going back, the bound is `before_ms` (EXCLUSIVE); going forward, `order=asc` reads from `since_ms` (then required). The trades routes add `after_id`, to resume inside one millisecond. Loop `while next: GET base + next`; it never repeats a row. A read that would exceed its time budget returns the rows it has with a `next` instead of failing, so a page can be shorter than `limit` (even empty) and still have a `next`: only `next: null` means the end. A 504 `upstream_timeout` remains possible on one very heavy page: reduce `limit`.
- **Freshness.** A response is usually up to one second old (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=1`); a cached copy can occasionally reach two seconds.
- **Strict parameters.** An undeclared or repeated parameter is a 422 with a suggestion (`limt` -> did you mean `limit`?), and so is an unknown value of a closed set (`symbol`, `asset`, `series`, `timeframe`, `category`, `ticker`, `expiry`…), with the accepted values in `error.details.accepted`. `symbol`, `asset`, `series`, `timeframe` and `order` are case-insensitive (`1M` excepted: elsewhere a month, here refused). `?fields=a,b.c` projects `data` (not on `POST /v1/indicators`, which takes no query parameter).
- **Aggregation only.** No route discloses which venue a number came from, except the inter-venue spread, whose purpose is to compare venues.
- **Browsers and probes.** The REST API answers CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, the `X-API-KEY` header allowed, preflight `OPTIONS` without a key) and `HEAD` on every `GET` route. A key used in a web page is readable by its visitors: use a dedicated key there.

## Errors

Every error has one shape, on the REST API and on the WebSocket (`{"op": "error", "server_time", "error": {...}}`):

```
{"status": "error", "server_time": "2026-10-13T08:00:00.000Z",
 "error": {"code": "invalid_symbol", "param": "symbol",
           "message": "Unknown symbol 'BTCUSD'. Did you mean 'BTCUSDT'? Accepted values: ...",
           "details": {"suggestion": "BTCUSDT", "accepted": ["ADAUSDT", "..."]}}}
```

Branch on `error.code` (stable, listed in the `ApiError` schema), show `error.message` (English), read `error.details` (an object, present when the error carries structured data) for what to change. A missing key is `missing_api_key`, a wrong one `invalid_api_key` (401). Key and plan refusals carry the same code in an `X-Deny-Reason` header (the edge anti-flood 429 `edge_rate_limited` carries none); 429 and 503 carry `Retry-After` (the real delay: until the next request of your rate, or the 1st of the month for the quota), always equal to `error.details.retry_after_s`.

## Limits

Each plan has a per-minute rate, a monthly quota and a history window per timeframe; `GET /v1/limits` returns those of your key. Responses made with a metered key carry the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers (policies `rate` and `quota`). Going further back than your plan allows is a 403 `history_depth`, never a silently truncated answer. Details: https://bytnode.com/docs/rate-limits.

## Versioning

The URL prefix `/v1` is the API generation. `info.version` is the revision of THIS contract, in semantic versioning: a PATCH corrects (a text, a value, a nullable field), a MINOR adds (a route, a field, a parameter, an accepted value), a MAJOR removes, renames or changes a meaning. Every response carries it in the `BytNode-Contract-Version` header, and each published version stays readable at `https://api.bytnode.com/openapi/<version>.json` (the list: `https://api.bytnode.com/openapi/index.json`). 2.0.0 (2026-10-16) is the reference version of this contract. The guide: https://bytnode.com/docs/versioning.

## Machine-readable files

This contract (`/openapi.json`, OpenAPI 3.1), the same in OpenAPI 3.0 (`/openapi-3.0.json`), a light copy without examples for AI agents (`/openapi-lite.json`), the WebSocket in AsyncAPI 3.0 (`/asyncapi.json`), and every published version (`/openapi/<version>.json`, listed in `/openapi/index.json`), all on https://api.bytnode.com, without a key. `GET /` (no key) returns the index of these links in the standard envelope (`data_type: index`, `data.contract_version`); it is a pointer to this contract, not a data route, so it is not listed under `paths`.

## Links

Docs https://bytnode.com/docs · Pricing https://bytnode.com/pricing · Full reference for LLMs https://bytnode.com/llms-full.txt · WebSocket `wss://ws.bytnode.com/ws` · MCP `https://api.bytnode.com/mcp` · Contact contact@bytnode.com

tags.name: System
tags.description: Health, per-feed freshness, the list of served symbols and what each symbol supports. `/v1/health` is the only route that needs no key.

tags.name: Snapshot
tags.description: One request, up to 48 fields for one symbol: the fastest way to fill a dashboard or give an AI agent full market context. Each field is `name=depth` (`funding_rate=1`, or `true` for depth 1); multi-timeframe fields are `name@tf=depth` (`klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`). Call it with only `symbol` to list the fields your plan includes.

tags.name: Market: prices & volumes
tags.description: OHLCV candles, individual trades, price change and the aggregated order book. OHLC comes from one reference spot market per symbol; a candle's `volume` covers spot and perpetual futures, `volume_spot` and `volume_futures` one market each.

tags.name: Order flow
tags.description: Who is buying and who is selling: trade candles (`trades-kline`: spot, futures, combined), CVD, buy/sell ratio, average trade size and inter-venue spread. Every bucketed series says whether the value is final (`is_closed`).

tags.name: Derivatives
tags.description: Perpetual futures positioning, aggregated across venues: funding (settled, estimated, cumulative), basis, open interest.

tags.name: Liquidations
tags.description: Forced liquidations across venues: individual events, cumulative long/short USD, big vs small liquidations, and the liquidation heatmap clusters the price is drawn to.

tags.name: Tokenomics & sentiment
tags.description: Supply, market cap and FDV derived from the live price; total crypto market cap and dominance; the Crypto Fear & Greed Index.

tags.name: Macro
tags.description: Daily FRED series (rates, inflation, liquidity, commodities, the VIX, US indices), intraday macro candles (ICE dollar index, EUR/USD, USD/JPY, gold, WTI oil), and derived crypto-macro signals: net liquidity, BTC correlations, macro momentum, risk-on/risk-off score.

tags.name: ETF
tags.description: Spot BTC and ETH ETF fundamentals per issuer, anchored on SEC EDGAR filings: shares, NAV, net assets and coins held.

tags.name: Options
tags.description: BTC and ETH options aggregated across venues: open interest and volume (calls/puts, USD), put/call ratio, ATM implied volatility, max pain, per-expiry and per-strike views, OI-weighted greeks.

tags.name: Bitcoin network
tags.description: Bitcoin chain state: recommended fees, mempool, mining pool concentration, difficulty and the next adjustment.

tags.name: Ethereum
tags.description: Ethereum fundamentals: gas, supply and burn, staking and yield, DeFi TVL, ETH/BTC ratio and derived signals (deflation, supply squeeze, gas momentum).

tags.name: On-chain Bitcoin
tags.description: Daily on-chain valuation and activity: MVRV, NVT, active addresses, miner stress.

tags.name: Technical indicators
tags.description: 19 technical indicators computed server-side on the same candles as `/v1/klines`, several per request (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, ATR, Ichimoku...).

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code. Branch on it, never on the message. The known codes are the `ErrorCode` schema; a code added later is not a breaking change, so handle an unknown one as a generic error.

- `depth_too_large`: A depth (snapshot field, WebSocket order book channel) exceeds its documented maximum.
- `edge_rate_limited`: Too many requests from this IP address at the edge (anti-flood: 20 per second per address, bursts of 40). Retry after 1 second.
- `history_depth`: The requested history goes further back than your plan allows.
- `https_required`: Plain HTTP is refused: call the same URL over https://. A key sent over http:// travelled unencrypted: rotate it.
- `insufficient_data`: Not enough history to compute the requested indicator.
- `internal_error`: Unexpected server error. A retry with backoff may succeed; if it persists, report it with the response's X-Request-Id header.
- `invalid_api_key`: The API key is invalid or revoked (or, on the WebSocket, the token is invalid, expired or already used).
- `invalid_asset`: The asset is not served by this family. The error lists the accepted values.
- `invalid_channel`: WebSocket: the channel name is malformed or unknown; the error lists the accepted forms.
- `invalid_depth`: A depth (snapshot field, WebSocket order book channel) is not a positive integer.
- `invalid_indicator`: The POST /v1/indicators body is invalid (id, type or parameters).
- `invalid_message`: WebSocket: the message is not a readable JSON object.
- `invalid_parameter`: A parameter has an invalid type or value.
- `invalid_series`: The macro series does not exist. See the family's /series catalogue.
- `invalid_symbol`: The symbol is not served. The error lists the accepted values (see /v1/symbols).
- `invalid_time_range`: since_ms / until_ms are not valid epoch milliseconds, or since_ms > until_ms (until_ms is inclusive).
- `invalid_timeframe`: The timeframe is not accepted by this route.
- `method_not_allowed`: The route exists but not with this HTTP method.
- `missing_api_key`: No API key was sent: put it in the X-API-KEY header (or api_key in the WebSocket URL).
- `missing_parameter`: A required parameter is missing.
- `not_applicable`: WebSocket: the channel has no meaning for this asset (a futures channel of a stablecoin). The REST API answers such a request with 200 and `unavailable: not_applicable`.
- `not_authenticated`: WebSocket: a message other than auth arrived on a session not yet authenticated (residual: the key is checked at the handshake, where a missing key answers 401 missing_api_key and an unknown or revoked one 401 invalid_api_key).
- `not_found`: Unknown route.
- `plan_family`: Your plan does not include this data family: the message names it, and GET /v1/limits lists the families of your key.
- `plan_websocket`: Your plan does not include the WebSocket stream.
- `quota_exceeded`: Your plan's monthly quota is exhausted. Retry-After (and retry_after) give the seconds until it resets, on the first day of the month (UTC).
- `rate_limited`: Your plan's per-minute rate is exceeded. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `repeated_parameter`: A parameter appears more than once.
- `service_unavailable`: Temporary unavailability. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `timeframe_not_served`: The series exists but does not serve this timeframe (a daily-only series asked in 1h). A timeframe the route never serves is invalid_timeframe.
- `unknown_field`: A ?fields= or snapshot field name does not exist.
- `unknown_parameter`: The route does not declare this parameter.
- `upstream_timeout`: The request took too long. Reduce the window or depth, then retry.

param.description: The parameter at fault, when there is one.

details.description: Structured complement, for code (absent when there is none). ALWAYS an object, with, when the error carries them: `suggestion` (the closest accepted value: `Did you mean`), `accepted` (the accepted values or parameters), `window_s`, `earliest_ms`, `max_limit` and `timeframe` (403 `history_depth`: your plan's window and the furthest bound it allows), `retry_after_s` (429 and 503: the seconds to wait, the same as `Retry-After`), `errors` (several validation errors: one `{param, message}` each).
details.title: ErrorDetails

suggestion.description: The closest accepted value (`Did you mean`).

max_limit.description: The largest `limit` your plan allows here.

window_s.description: Your plan's history window for this timeframe, in seconds.

earliest_ms.description: The furthest bound your plan allows, at the time of the response (epoch ms).

timeframe.description: The timeframe the window applies to.

retry_after_s.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (the same as the `Retry-After` header).

errors.description: Every validation error of the request, one `{param, message}` each.

error.description: The error: `code`, `message`, `param` when one parameter is at fault, `details`.

Asset.description: Underlying asset of the options and spot ETF routes.

time.description: Point-in-time value: the instant of the venue prices used (each venue's last futures and spot trades, at most 2 minutes old).

basis_value.description: Futures price - spot price, in the quote currency (USDT for BTCUSDT), like the two prices.

basis_pct.description: (futures - spot) / spot, in percent. Positive = contango.

futures_price.description: Perpetual futures price, open-interest weighted across venues.

spot_price.description: Spot price across venues at the instant of the row, paired with the futures price of the same instant. Not the latest trade price: that is the `price` of `/v1/price-change`, i.e. the close of `/v1/klines?live=1`.

time.description: Start of the bucket of `timeframe`; the value is the LAST one of the bucket's minutes.

basis_value.description: Futures price - spot price, in the quote currency (USDT for BTCUSDT), like the two prices.

basis_pct.description: (futures - spot) / spot, in percent. Positive = contango.

futures_price.description: Perpetual futures price, open-interest weighted across venues.

spot_price.description: Spot price across venues at the instant of the row, paired with the futures price of the same instant. Not the latest trade price: that is the `price` of `/v1/price-change`, i.e. the close of `/v1/klines?live=1`.

sample_count.description: Number of source points in the bucket (one-minute points with data). For a state (basis, open interest) the value is the LAST of them — the bucket's close —; for a flow it is their total.

is_closed.description: `true` = the row is final; `false` = provisional: the latest bucket while it still settles (a few seconds after its end, e.g. a candle whose volumes are not final yet), or the period in progress with `?live=1` on the routes that take it. Exception, rare: when a venue delivers trades LATE (seconds to minutes, e.g. during a burst), a closed row built from trades (trade candles, candle volumes, CVD, buy/sell ratio, trades per second) is corrected afterwards to include them, usually within minutes and at most one hour later; the correction only adds the late trades.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

data_type.description: Name of the payload type: the route's own name (stable).

step.description: Step between two rows of `data`: the `timeframe` you asked for on a route that takes one, otherwise the cadence of the series. A BUCKET row is dated at the start of its bucket (aligned: `14:00:00.000Z` in `1h`); a row of a periodic READING (Bitcoin fees, mempool and network, mining pools) is dated at the instant of the reading, `step` apart (`08:19:08.316Z`, then `08:18:08.297Z` in `1m`). Absent when the rows have no fixed step (one row per publication or per block, a monthly series).

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

next.description: The relative URL of the following page, ready to call (`GET https://api.bytnode.com` + `next`): your parameters, with the page bound set. It never repeats a row. `null` once the range is read. Follow it until it is `null`: a page can hold fewer rows than `limit` (even none) and still have a `next` — an ascending read that reaches a dense period returns, within its time budget, what it has read so far.

unavailable.description: Present only when `data` is empty: why.

buy_volume.description: Aggressive (taker) buy volume, base asset units, aggregated across venues.

sell_volume.description: Aggressive (taker) sell volume, base asset units, aggregated across venues.

sample_count.description: Number of points of the CVD series behind the bucket — the `sample_count` of `/v1/cvd/history` for the same bucket.

buy_sell_coverage_ratio.description: Share of the volume (in USD) whose buy/sell split is known. 1 = every trade is split. Below 1 on part of the history, where some sources did not report the aggressor side: `buy_volume` and `sell_volume` then cover that share only, so `buy_volume + sell_volume` < `volume`; `buy_ratio` and the CVD describe the covered share. `null` when the bucket has no volume.

is_volume_estimated.description: `true` when base-asset quantities of this row were ESTIMATED from USD amounts ÷ the candle's typical price (high + low + close) / 3 (data written before quantities were recorded; mean error 0.04 % in 1m, 0.37 % in 1d); `false` = measured. `null` when the volume itself is `null` (not available).

is_closed.description: `true` = the row is final; `false` = provisional: the latest bucket while it still settles (a few seconds after its end, e.g. a candle whose volumes are not final yet), or the period in progress with `?live=1` on the routes that take it. Exception, rare: when a venue delivers trades LATE (seconds to minutes, e.g. during a burst), a closed row built from trades (trade candles, candle volumes, CVD, buy/sell ratio, trades per second) is corrected afterwards to include them, usually within minutes and at most one hour later; the correction only adds the late trades.

data_type.description: Name of the payload type: the route's own name (stable).

market.description: Market served, from the route path: `all` (no suffix: spot + perpetual futures), `spot` (`/spot`) or `futures` (`/futures`).

step.description: Step between two rows of `data`: the `timeframe` you asked for on a route that takes one, otherwise the cadence of the series. A BUCKET row is dated at the start of its bucket (aligned: `14:00:00.000Z` in `1h`); a row of a periodic READING (Bitcoin fees, mempool and network, mining pools) is dated at the instant of the reading, `step` apart (`08:19:08.316Z`, then `08:18:08.297Z` in `1m`). Absent when the rows have no fixed step (one row per publication or per block, a monthly series).

Exception, rare: when a venue delivers trades LATE (seconds to minutes, e.g. during a burst), a closed row built from trades (trade candles, candle volumes, CVD, buy/sell ratio, trades per second) is corrected afterwards to include them, usually within minutes and at most one hour later; the correction only adds the late trades.

range_pct.description: Half-width of the range around each venue's mid price ((best bid + best ask) / 2): `1.0` = bids down to -1 % and asks up to +1 %.

bids_quantity.description: Resting BUY orders inside the range (price >= mid × (1 - range_pct/100)), summed across venues. `null` = no venue publishes its book that deep.

asks_quantity.description: Resting SELL orders inside the range (price <= mid × (1 + range_pct/100)), summed across venues. `null` = not measured.

bids_usd.description: USD value (Σ price × quantity) of the buy orders inside the range.

asks_usd.description: USD value (Σ price × quantity) of the sell orders inside the range.

imbalance_ratio.description: (bids_usd - asks_usd) / (bids_usd + asks_usd). Positive = more bids than asks. `null` when one side is not measured.

ranges.description: One entry per price range around the mid price, from the tightest (±0.25 %) to the widest (±10 %). Each range is cumulative: ±1 % includes everything inside ±0.5 %.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

data_type.description: Name of the payload type: the route's own name (stable).

market.description: Market served, from the route path: `all` (no suffix: spot + perpetual futures), `spot` (`/spot`) or `futures` (`/futures`).

step.description: Step between two rows of `data`: the `timeframe` you asked for on a route that takes one, otherwise the cadence of the series. A BUCKET row is dated at the start of its bucket (aligned: `14:00:00.000Z` in `1h`); a row of a periodic READING (Bitcoin fees, mempool and network, mining pools) is dated at the instant of the reading, `step` apart (`08:19:08.316Z`, then `08:18:08.297Z` in `1m`). Absent when the rows have no fixed step (one row per publication or per block, a monthly series).

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

next.description: The relative URL of the following page, ready to call (`GET https://api.bytnode.com` + `next`): your parameters, with the page bound set. It never repeats a row. `null` once the range is read. Follow it until it is `null`: a page can hold fewer rows than `limit` (even none) and still have a `next` — an ascending read that reaches a dense period returns, within its time budget, what it has read so far.

time.description: Start of the bucket the row covers: a 1h bucket at 14:00 covers 14:00:00 to 14:59:59.999.

is_closed.description: `true` = the row is final; `false` = provisional: the latest bucket while it still settles (a few seconds after its end, e.g. a candle whose volumes are not final yet), or the period in progress with `?live=1` on the routes that take it. Exception, rare: when a venue delivers trades LATE (seconds to minutes, e.g. during a burst), a closed row built from trades (trade candles, candle volumes, CVD, buy/sell ratio, trades per second) is corrected afterwards to include them, usually within minutes and at most one hour later; the correction only adds the late trades.

weighting.description: How venues are combined: `oi` (open-interest weighted) or `volume` (volume weighted).

max_spread_bps.description: Gap between the highest and the lowest venue price, relative to ref_price.

high_venue.description: Venue with the highest price over the bucket.

high_price.description: Its volume-weighted price over the bucket.

low_venue.description: Venue with the lowest price over the bucket.

low_price.description: Its volume-weighted price over the bucket.

venue.description: Venue name (this route is the only one that names venues).

price.description: Volume-weighted price of the venue over the bucket.

premium_bps.description: Venue price premium (positive) or discount (negative) versus ref_price.

get.description: One row per closed bucket of `timeframe` (required). Each `timeframe` starts where readings are at least that fine, so `step` is always the real spacing: `1d` covers the whole history, `4h` starts on 2025-10-07, `1h` on 2026-04-04 17:00 UTC, and `1m` to `30m` on 2026-05-28 19:10 UTC (2026-09-12 14:40 UTC for AVAX, HBAR, LINK, NEAR, TAO, UNI, XMR, ADA, GRAM and LTC; older readings were taken once a day, then every 4 hours, then hourly). Read older periods at a coarser `timeframe`; a `since_ms` before the start is raised to it, and a window entirely before it returns no rows. Most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`. Follow `next` to read the following page (it never repeats a row).

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Lower time bound, INCLUSIVE, in epoch MILLISECONDS (13 digits). A value in seconds returns 422 `invalid_time_range`.

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, INCLUSIVE to the millisecond, in epoch milliseconds. To page, prefer `before_ms` (exclusive) or simply follow `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows to return, in the reading order (most recent first by default). Bounded by your plan's history window: an explicit `limit` (or `since_ms`) reaching beyond it returns 403 `history_depth`; without them the page simply stops at the window.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: Required: `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h` or `1d`. One row per closed bucket: for a STATE (basis, open interest, heatmap) the value of its LAST minute — its close —, for a FLOW (open-interest change, liquidations, trade sizes) the total over its minutes; `sample_count` = minutes with data in the bucket. `1m` gives one row per minute, aligned on the minute. Missing: 422 `missing_parameter`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required. The 22 served pairs: `GET /v1/symbols`. Case-insensitive (`btcusdt` works; the envelope gives the canonical `BTCUSDT`). An unknown pair returns 422 `invalid_symbol` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection of `data` (dot notation for nested keys): `fields=time,basis_value`. Unknown field: 422 `unknown_field` with a suggestion.

parameters.name: before_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, EXCLUSIVE, in epoch milliseconds: rows strictly before it. Pass the oldest `time` you received to read the previous page without repeating a row. Not combinable with `until_ms` (422 `invalid_time_range`).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Reading order: `desc` (most recent first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first, reading forward from `since_ms`, which is then required). Follow `next` to read the following page.

get.summary: Many fields for one symbol in one request
get.description: 48 fields for one symbol in a single call (40 plain, 8 multi-timeframe): prices, flow, derivatives, liquidations, macro, on-chain, options. Each query key is a field and its value a depth: `funding_rate=1` (or `=true`). Multi-timeframe fields take `@tf`: `klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`; `klines` also takes `1w`. Every field has the name of its route, and ONE type whatever the depth: a field WITHOUT a timeframe is the response of its latest-value route, an object (depth 1, or `true`; 422 `depth_too_large` above, naming its `/history` route) — except the event series `trades_spot`, `trades_futures`, `trades_kline_futures_seconds` and `liquidations_events`, always a list of their latest N rows; a field WITH `@tf` is ALWAYS a list, the latest N rows of its `/history` at that timeframe (`cvd@1h=1` is a list of one row). `max_depth` gives each ceiling. The timeframe is case-insensitive like everywhere (`cvd@1H`), except `1M`. A market field serves all markets (the route without `/spot` or `/futures`). Call it with only `symbol` to get, under `data`, `available_fields` (fields without a timeframe), `available_multi_tf_fields`, `multi_tf_syntax`, `timeframes`, `timeframes_by_field` and `max_depth`. An empty field carries `unavailable` (`not_applicable`, `no_api_key` or `no_data`) so 'no measure' is never mistaken for 'nothing happened'. Response: `symbol`, `data` (an object keyed by field name) and `is_partial` (true if a field failed: that field is then an `error` object with `code` and `message`, with the codes of the error catalogue).

post.description: For a BROWSER (or any client you do not trust with your API key): your server calls this route with its key in the `X-API-KEY` header and hands the browser only the token, which opens the stream at `wss://ws.bytnode.com/ws?token=…`. The key never reaches the page, and nothing long-lived ends up in a URL (browser history, proxy logs). A token lasts 60 seconds and opens ONE connection: once used, or expired, it is refused (401 `invalid_api_key`, with a message saying so); request a new one for each connection or reconnection. It opens the WebSocket only, never a REST route. Same right as the stream itself: a plan without the WebSocket gets 403 `plan_websocket`. Not counted in your monthly quota (your per-minute rate applies). The rights are those of your key at the moment of the handshake: a key revoked in between no longer connects. Server-side code can keep sending the key in the `X-API-KEY` header of the handshake (or `?api_key=`); the token is the form meant for web pages.
